Computational philology / exploratory atlas

How long is a book of Livy?

A structural fingerprint of the 35 substantially surviving books of Ab Urbe Condita, including word counts, editorial sections, approximate sentences, and Latin vocabulary frequency.

504,578Latin word tokens
14,950Mean tokens per book, 1–40
20,296Editorial section units
20,997Estimated sentences
Scope. Surviving books only: I–X, XXI–XLV. Books XI–XX are lost, not represented by ancient summaries. Textual lacunae in Books XLI–XLV make their lengths severe underestimates. Word counts are edition- and tokenizer-dependent.

01 / Volume is not uniform

Across the 30 surviving books numbered 1–40, counts range from 10,665 (Book 32) to 20,207 (Book 3). A 15,000-word target is a useful weak prior, not a rigid rule for lost texts.

02 / Prose structure is somewhat steadier

The encoded <p> units map largely to classical numbered sections, not necessarily paragraphs authored by Livy. Average sentence length is punctuation-derived, and sensitive to abbreviations and editorial punctuation.

03 / The vocabulary has a long tail

Across all 35 books there are approximately 51,294 distinct case-sensitive-normalized-to-lowercase word forms, of which about 25,250 occur once (~49%). This is un-lemmatized Latin: inflections and proper names inflate the number of forms. Function words dominate frequency, as expected.

04 / All 35 books

“Lacuna” marks explicit <gap reason="lost"/> occurrences in this TEI; zero does not establish textual completeness. “Types/1k” is mean unique forms in non-overlapping windows of 1,000 tokens per book.

05 / What this can—and cannot—reconstruct

Use the length distribution as a broad volume prior, compare within narrative regimes, and validate on surviving books by hiding complete text from the reconstruction system. Do not use word frequency or sentence-length statistics to generate purported original wording, and do not treat the Periochae as proportional miniatures of their lost books.

Surviving derivatives can support a historical event skeleton, not a verbatim recreation of Livy's prose. For each inferred event, preserve source provenance and independence. Compare held-out events, order, and uncertainty calibration before relying on stylistic shape.

Methods & provenance

Source: Perseus Digital Library TEI (Weissenborn–Müller edition), phi0914.phi001.perseus-lat2.xml; Book entries with numeric identifiers only (1–10, 21–45), excluding interleaved Periochae entries with suffix “s.” Count only text within paragraph tags; editorial choices prefer corrected readings; deletions and notes excluded. Unicode letter-token counting; abbreviations masked for a heuristic sentence segmentation. A historical edition's periods, sections and corrections are editorial decisions. Last five books have major transmission losses. The CSV contains the per-book summaries.
